newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares cautious ahead of company results.
newsitem.headline: India shares cautious ahead of company results.

text.p: Indian stocks, hit by a sharp sell-off the previous day, treaded cautiously on Thursday ahead of first-half results of top firms, brokers and analysts said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top-30 share index was down 25.97 points, or 0.82 percent, at 3,147.01 in afternoon trade after sliding to 3,122.76.
Wednesday's market drop was sparked by the arrests of former leading tobacco conglomerate executives.
"The panic has subsided," said BSE member-broker Ramesh Damani. "Players are nervous about TISCO results."

Tata Iron and Steel Company Ltd (TISCO), the flagship of the Tata industrial group, was to release its results for the first six months to September 30 only after trading ends for the day, a company official said.
TISCO shares were down 6.50 rupees at 180.25 in afternoon trade at the BSE.

The market took a pounding on Wednesday after India's Enforcement Directorate arrested a director and three former officials of tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC Ltd for alleged violations of foreign exchange rules.

"The search operations were organised...only after sufficient evidence had been collected indicating FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million," the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
ITC was up 0.75 rupees at 303.75 on Thursday afternoon after tumbling 5.68 percent on Wednesday.
"It is a good time to buy ITC," said Sujay Mishra, company analyst at SSKI Securities. "Crises like this offer buy opportunities at cheap valuations."
He said the arrests related to "past practices" when the tobacco conglomerate ventured into agricultural exports that have since been discontinued.
ITC is 31.7 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc The rest of its shares are held by Indian financial institutions and the public.
"The market fell yesterday in sympathy with ITC," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share and Stock Brokers. "I see no further damage."
He said some players' fears about company results were misplaced and he expected to see a rebound.
Scooter maker Bajaj Auto said its net profit for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) rose 27.68 percent to 2.26 billion rupees against 1.77 billion in year-ago period.
Bajaj Auto shares rose 14.75 rupees to 956.25 soon after the announcement.
